issues.issue: The defined term "Defendants" sweeps in "proposed additional defendants" (Santa Fe Auto Insurance Company and James Thornton Maxwell), who were not yet parties to the Lawsuit, leaving it unclear whether they are bound as "Parties" and on what claims. The phrase "these original and proposed additional defendants" has no boundary and no mechanism for their joinder.

This paragraph's party list cannot be squared with Section VI of the Memorandum of Understanding, which describes the same instrument as the "April 28, 2008 letter agreement between Lincoln General, U.S. Auto, Gamma, CSi, Alpha, and Doug Maxwell" — omitting Santa Fe and Jim Maxwell, who appear here and in the signature block. The date discrepancy (letter dated April 30) compounds the identification problem.

The paragraph is framed as a limitation ("agrees to limit the scope of its claims ... to the following") but each enumerated category is opened up again by catch-alls — "This includes, but is not limited to," "among other things," and "other persons or entities" — so the general language arguably swallows the enumerated specifics. A court would have to decide whether ejusdem generis confines the retained claims to the listed IBNR-commission and improper-payment theories.

Category (2) (paying or overpaying claims on policies not reinsured or only partially reinsured, out of a Lincoln General-funded account) overlaps with the claims excluded by the "Other Causes of Action" paragraph, which bars claims for "mishandling of insurance claims on the reinsured policies." Which paragraph governs a claim that sounds in both is not resolved.

"Other Causes of Action" is defined by an exhaustive list of four items with an embedded carve-out ("other than concerning the exclusion or misapplication of IBNR"), so any claim that is neither on this list nor within the retained-claims paragraph falls into a gap the agreement does not allocate. Whether the enumeration is exclusive (expressio unius) is left open.

The bar on "mishandling of insurance claims on the reinsured policies" cannot be squared with the retained claim in the limitation paragraph for improper or excess payments of insurance claims out of a Lincoln General-funded account. The same conduct can be characterised as falling on either side of the line.

The reservation of a right to assert the Other Causes of Action "as part of a separate lawsuit" stands against the immediately following sentence forbidding any such separate lawsuit from being filed during the pendency of the Lawsuit, and against Section VI of the Memorandum of Understanding, which tolls those same claims for five years. Whether the reserved right survives, and for how long, depends on reading the three together.

"During the pendency of the Lawsuit" is undefined and has no stated end point — in particular whether a dismissal without prejudice (as contemplated by Section V of the Memorandum of Understanding) ends pendency, or whether appeals must first be exhausted as the tolling paragraphs separately require. The provision also states no consequence for a filing made in breach.

The temporal trigger here ("pendency of the Lawsuit") does not match the trigger in the Defendants' tolling paragraph for the same Other Causes of Action ("settled or otherwise finally resolved, including the completion of any appeals"), so the filing bar and the tolling period may not be coextensive. A gap or overlap between the two would have to be construed.

"Agrees to enable ... to limit the claims it might otherwise seek" states no obligation of anyone: it neither identifies which claims U.S. Auto is limiting nor imposes any duty on U.S. Auto to limit them, unlike the parallel Lincoln General limitation paragraph. "Enable" is vague as to what Lincoln General is actually promising.

The Excess Funds Claim(s) are defined by reference to "the maximum profit margin to which U.S. Auto contends Lincoln General is entitled" — a standard fixed by one party's own contention rather than by any ascertainable figure or contract term, and expanded by "including, but not limited to a breach of contract claim." The parenthetical definition is also left unclosed, so the boundary of the defined term is textually uncertain.

The concession that the Excess Funds Claim(s) do not arise from the same nucleus of operative facts as the Lawsuit sits uneasily with the retained-claims paragraph, which keeps in the Lawsuit claims about amounts allegedly owing to and improperly retained from Lincoln General under the same reinsurance arrangement. Whether the two descriptions can both be true of the same monies is a question the agreement forces.

The express waiver of res judicata and collateral estoppel cannot be squared with the final paragraph, in which Lincoln General and Defendants "all reserve the right to contest any later-filed separate lawsuits, and may assert any and all applicable defenses or affirmative defenses." Which provision controls a preclusion defense in the Excess Funds suit is unresolved.

"Until the Lawsuit has been settled or otherwise finally resolved, including the completion of any appeals" is ambiguous as applied to a dismissal without prejudice, which resolves nothing on the merits and generates no appeal — the very disposition Section V of the Memorandum of Understanding contemplates. The duplicated "for the the" aside, nothing fixes when the toll ends.

The reservation of "any limitations defenses which may exist immediately before this agreement is executed" pulls against the tolling promise in the preceding sentence, and no execution date is fixed anywhere in the letter (the letterhead says April 30, 2008 while the Memorandum of Understanding calls it the April 28, 2008 letter agreement). A court would have to decide as of what date the preserved defenses are measured.

"During the pendency of the Lawsuit" is undefined, and the provision does not say whether pendency ends on a dismissal without prejudice or only on final resolution including appeals, as the tolling sentence two lines earlier phrases it. It also prescribes no consequence for a suit filed in breach of the bar.

The flat prohibition on filing conflicts with the permission granted earlier in the same paragraph that "U.S. Auto may, in a separate lawsuit, assert" the Excess Funds Claim(s). The two must be reconciled to determine whether the right is granted or merely deferred.

Defendants' concession that the Other Causes of Action do not share a nucleus of operative facts with the Lawsuit is hard to square with the definition of those causes of action, which concerns handling, reserves and closing of claims on the very reinsured policies at issue in the retained claims. Whether the parties can contract around the factual overlap is left to construction.

The express waiver of res judicata and collateral estoppel as to the Other Causes of Action conflicts with the closing paragraph, in which all parties "reserve the right to contest any later-filed separate lawsuits, and may assert any and all applicable defenses or affirmative defenses." The instrument does not say which prevails.

This tolling of the Other Causes of Action "until the Lawsuit has been settled or otherwise finally resolved" cannot be squared with Section VI of the Memorandum of Understanding, which tolls the same "Other Causes of Action" for five years or until all claims on the subject policies are paid and settled. The two agreements fix different tolling end points for identical claims.

"Settled or otherwise finally resolved, including the completion of any appeals" gives no answer for a dismissal without prejudice, which neither settles nor finally resolves the Lawsuit yet ends it. The end date of the toll is therefore indeterminate.

Defendants' reservation of "any limitations defenses which may exist immediately before this agreement is executed" is in tension with their tolling promise in the preceding sentence, and the agreement fixes no execution date against which pre-existing defenses can be measured. Whether limitations that had partly run are preserved or suspended is unresolved.

The qualifier "by entering into this agreement, in general" is vague: it is unclear whether "in general" limits the non-concession to some acts and not others, or is mere surplusage. The scope of what Defendants are declining to concede therefore has no fixed boundary.

The provision uses "Excess Fund Claim(s)" whereas the term defined earlier in the letter is "the Excess Funds Claim(s)," a mechanical mismatch in the defined term. It is a small point, but it leaves the referent of this sentence technically undefined.

The blanket reservation of "any and all applicable defenses or affirmative defenses" cannot be squared with the two earlier paragraphs in which Lincoln General and Defendants expressly relinquish and waive res judicata and collateral estoppel as to the Excess Funds Claim(s) and Other Causes of Action. Whether "applicable" silently excludes the waived preclusion defenses is precisely what would be argued.
